newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end day firm, aided by Wall St gains.
newsitem.headline: German shares end day firm, aided by Wall St gains.

text.p: German shares got the week off to a strong start on Monday, gaining around one percent over the day amid healthy interest in blue chip auto companies and as Wall Street built further on its gains from Friday.

The blue chip DAX-30 index rose 22.04 points to 2,881,32 points in bourse dealings and the IBIS DAX, which tracks all-day electronic dealings, extended those gains to end the day up 26.94 points, or 0.94 percent, at 2,890.20.

Initial gains were triggered by a 1.6 percent rise on the Dow Jones on Friday and news which attracted interest to auto giants such as Daimler-Benz and VW. Later gains were spurred by fresh gains in early trade on Wall Street.
Volumes were weak, however, because a public holiday in southern Germany kept several large banks out of the market.

"This has been a difficult day because of the low volumes but there are many factors at home to justify an uptrend and I think they will win," said one Frankfurt dealer, who said jobless and GDP data due on Thursday would be closely eyed.

Daimler-Benz rose 3.50 marks to 109.30 over the day after its Mercedes unit, which accounts for most of parent company profits, told journalists in Detroit it expected 1997 U.S. sales at over 100,000 units.
More gains came after its Airbus joint venture unit said it would raise its output by 45 percent in 1997.

Volkswagen rose 8.75 marks to 650 marks as dealers said they were confident of more data suggesting strong growth in the sector over the rest of the week. VW was also boosted by a report it was planning this year to build a new "mini-car" to compete in the small-car market, dealer said.
But BMW slid 2.85 to 1,053.15 marks, which dealers attributed simply to the comparative lack of interesting news on the company.
Diversified utility Veba AG was another strong gainer, rising 1.77 marks to 91.25 after it revealed an acquisition to boost its cable television activities.
The group's Vebacom unit bought Urbana Systemtechnick in a deal which will increase its share of the German cable TV market from the current seven percent to 10 percent.
